body: This looks sensible imo, even if slightly harder to read, it emphasises there is a big performance penalty to making copies of `LocalVector`.

As we discussed in the core meeting, I am all in favour of using explicit copy constructors to help us avoid accidentally copying an entire LocalVector. I think it makes a lot of sense for our commonly used containers. 

In this case it is extra useful since it helps highlight when LocalVectors are being passed around. As the name implies, they shouldn't really be passed around to wider contexts and are meant to stay local to the class they are declared in. So seeing them get copied and moved around makes it easier for us to notice when they really should be using a Vector or other container with COW
